Package gui

This package contains 242 source unit(s) defining 243 class(es) / struct(s). Each unit below lists its fields (the values it stores) and methods (the actions it performs), with a plain explanation of each.

gui-app-demo #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/gui-app-demo.sleela)

GuiAppDemo class

Runnable demonstrator for the /lib/gui support structure. It boots an SLGuiApp (application + window + DOM + reconciler + host adapter + script engine), builds a small interface in the SLeeLa DOM, binds an onClick callback, drives part of the UI from a script, refreshes once to project the DOM onto real SleelaUI widgets, and (on a display) hands control to the run loop. On a headless host boot() returns false and it exits cleanly, like gui-demo.sleela. This proves the architectural wiring end to end: DOM -> reconcile -> widgets, and widget activations -> events -> handlers. Family: gui. SLeeLa owns the document and dispatch; SleelaUI renders it.

gui-events-demo #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/gui-events-demo.sleela)

GuiEventsDemo class

Runnable demonstrator for the /lib/gui event + DHTML + scripting layer. It builds a small document (a window with a button and an entry), binds callbacks (onClick / onInput) the DHTML way, raises events and shows the dispatcher routing them to operations with the take-the-latch latch, demonstrates preventDefault/stopPropagation, mutates the DOM live (setText/setStyle/hide), and finally drives the SAME interface from an SLGuiScript command list — proving the UI can be authored and driven by scripting. Self-contained (inline flow + main), in the style of gui-demo.sleela. Family: gui. SLeeLa owns dispatch and the meaning of events; a host only raises them and mirrors the DOM onto widgets.

gui-guide-chain-demo #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-mual/gui-guide-chain-demo.sleela)

GuiGuideChainDemo class

Runnable demonstrator for the philosophers Guide-chain operator (syntax 2.3, SLEELA.syntax section 17) applied to GUI setup. A window is "constructed and guided" in one expression: new GuiPanel() :: window :: title :: listen :: show where each Guide is a zero-argument setup step applied in order, and the chain evaluates to the constructed panel (fluent). This is the gui-family reading of the perfect Constructor: the construction of a GUI surface IS a seated sequence of growths. Self-contained (inline model + main).

SLGuiAction class

Defines SLGuiAction — a named, bindable GUI action. Mirrors the SleelaGuiRuntime.action(name, operation) / SleelaGui.onAction(...) binding in gui/: a name the window raises and a SLeeLa operation it maps to. The VM latches each activation so a click (or Enter/Space while focused) is observed exactly once.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

FieldDeclarationWhat it holds
nameString namethe action's stable name
operationString operationthe SLeeLa operation it invokes
pendingint pendingactivation latch (set on raise, cleared on take)
firedint firedtotal activations observed

Methods — the actions this unit can perform.

MethodSignatureWhat it does
configurevoid configure(String n, String op)No description in source.
getNameString getName()No description in source.
getOperationString getOperation()No description in source.
boundboolean bound()No description in source.
raisevoid raise()The host raises an activation (a click, or Enter/Space while focused).
takeboolean take()Take-the-latch read: true once per activation, then cleared — the VM clears the latch on read, so each click is observed exactly once.
activationsint activations()No description in source.

SLGuiApp #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiApp.sleela)

SLGuiApp class

Defines SLGuiApp — the top-level support structure that ties the whole /lib/gui dynamic stack together into one object: it opens a SleelaUI application and window (via /lib/user-interface), owns the SLeeLa DOM (SLGuiDom), the reconciler (SLGuiMount) that projects the DOM onto widgets, the host adapter (SLGuiHostAdapter) that raises widget activations back as events, and an optional script engine (SLGuiScript). Its run loop pumps the toolkit event loop, polls widget activations into the event bus, re-mounts any newly-created nodes, and reconciles dirty nodes each turn. This is the "basic support structure" a program (or the IDE) builds on: construct the DOM declaratively or by script, bind callbacks, and call run(). Family: gui. SLeeLa owns the DOM, dispatch, and script execution; SleelaUI owns presentation; this object is the wiring between them.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

Fields — the named values this unit stores.

FieldDeclarationWhat it holds
THEME_PRESETstatic final int THEME_PRESET = SLTheme.DEFAULTChoose DEFAULT, WHITE, BLUE, BLACK, or GRAY here for this GUI family.
uiSLUserInterface uiNo description in source.
windowSLWindow windowNo description in source.
domSLGuiDom domNo description in source.
mountSLGuiMount mountNo description in source.
hostSLGuiHostAdapter hostNo description in source.
scriptSLGuiScript scriptNo description in source.
brandingSLGuiBranding branding3.0 logo/brand identity painted into the chrome
audioSLGuiAudioCues audio3.0 activation-audio cue registry
codecsSLGuiCodecs codecs4.0 codec registry (mirror of /codecs) GUI can see
htmlSLGuiHtmlRenderer html4.0 HTML/CSS/JS renderer (quick-responsive)
screenFitterSLGuiScreenFit screenFittersizes the window from the actual screen size
frameMillisint frameMillisnominal per-loop tick for scheduled effects
readyint readyNo description in source.

Methods — the actions this unit can perform.

MethodSignatureWhat it does
bootboolean boot(String appId, String title, int width, int height)Open the application + window and stand up the DOM/mount/host wiring. Returns true when the toolkit came up (false on a headless host).
bootFittedboolean bootFitted(String appId, String title, int tier)Open the application and size the window to the ACTUAL screen / resolution, at a support tier (0=basic, 1=moderate, 2=advanced; see SLGuiScreenFit). Queries uiScreenWidth/uiScreenHeight through the facade; a headless host falls back to a modeled 1920x1080. Returns true when the toolkit came up.
screenFitSLGuiScreenFit screenFit()The screen-fit helper (primed with the real screen). Call setScreen()/fit() to recompute, then read width()/height()/x()/y() for a resize or re-center.
scrollbarForSLGuiScrollbar scrollbarFor(int viewport, int content, boolean horizontal)Build an IMPLIED scrollbar model for a scrolled surface. `horizontal` selects the axis; `viewport`/`content` are the extents on that axis. The returned SLGuiScrollbar yields orient()/valuePermille()/pagePermille() to paint with uiScrollBar (or an SLScrollBar), and tracks the scroll offset.
setBufferingvoid setBuffering(int mode)Presentation buffering for the live window: 0=single, 1=double (the toolkit default, flicker-free resize), 2=triple (smoother rapid resize). Pass SLGuiSettings.getBufferingMode() here to honor the configured knob.
bufferingint buffering()No description in source.
addScrolledSLGuiNode addScrolled(String parentId, String id)Add a SCROLLED VIEWPORT node to the DOM under `parentId`. Its children become the scroll content and native scrollbars appear AUTOMATICALLY when that content is larger than the viewport. Pin the viewport smaller than its content (e.g. style "min-height") to force scrolling. Equivalent to adding a "scrolled" element; returns the node so the caller can append content to it.
addOverflowBoxSLGuiNode addOverflowBox(String parentId, String id, String overflow)Add a plain container that scrolls on overflow by setting its `overflow` intent (auto|scroll|always|hidden). SLGuiMount promotes it to a native scrolled viewport. Returns the node for appending content.
transitionSLGuiTransition transition()---- fade / transition helpers ------------------------------------------ A reusable enter/exit fade primitive (the shared tween). Returns a default 200ms ease-out fade-in the caller can retarget with fadeIn/fadeOut/between.
toastSLGuiToast toast(String message)A TOAST / SNACKBAR: a small self-dismissing notification that fades in, dwells, and fades out. Driven by tick(); read opacityPct() to paint it.
modalSLGuiModal modal(String title)A MODAL / OVERLAY: a dialog that fades in over a darkened backdrop (scrim).
skeletonSLGuiSkeleton skeleton(int shape, int lines)A SKELETON SCREEN / PLACEHOLDER: a shimmering loading placeholder that dissolves to reveal real content (shape 0=text/1=card/2=avatar/3=list).
codecRegistrySLGuiCodecs codecRegistry()---- 4.0 codecs + HTML renderer access ---------------------------------- The codec registry every GUI media component can consult.
htmlRendererSLGuiHtmlRenderer htmlRenderer()No description in source.
canPlayCodecboolean canPlayCodec(String codecName)Convenience capability questions for GUI implementations.
canPlayExtensionboolean canPlayExtension(String ext)No description in source.
supportedCodecsint supportedCodecs()No description in source.
brandSLGuiBranding brand()---- 3.0 branding + audio access ----------------------------------------
audioCuesSLGuiAudioCues audioCues()No description in source.
setFrameMillisvoid setFrameMillis(int ms)No description in source.
setLogovoid setLogo(String asset, String accent)Apply a brand logo + accent in one call (host paints it into the chrome).
effectsForSLGuiEffects effectsFor(String nodeId)Give a node an effects bundle and (optionally) an activation cue, then flatten it into the node's style for the next reconcile.
isReadyboolean isReady()No description in source.
documentSLGuiDom document()No description in source.
scriptingSLGuiScript scripting()No description in source.
hostWindowSLWindow hostWindow()No description in source.
addSLGuiNode add(String parentId, String tag, String id)Convenience: append an element to a parent in the DOM (then mount+show on the next loop turn, or immediately via refresh()).
onClickSLGuiHandler onClick(String id, String operation)Bind a click callback (DHTML onClick) by node id.
runScriptint runScript()Run a UI script against the DOM (build + bind + fire), then refresh.
runint run()Mount everything, show the window, then run the toolkit event loop: pump -> poll activations -> mount new nodes -> reconcile. Returns the process-style exit code.
advanceEffectsint advanceEffects(int elapsedMillis)Advance every node's scheduled effects by `elapsedMillis`: scheduled rotations turn (and their bound memorandum key epoch rotates with them), and the host interpolates fades. Returns how many nodes moved this tick.
refreshvoid refresh()A single synchronous refresh (mount new + reconcile) without the loop, for building a UI up front or driving it from a test/host step.
stepint step(boolean block)Pump one turn (pump + poll + refresh); returns events raised this turn.
quitvoid quit(int code)No description in source.
shutdownvoid shutdown()No description in source.

SLGuiApp class

Defines SLGuiApp — the top-level support structure that ties the whole /lib/gui dynamic stack together into one object: it opens a SleelaUI application and window (via /lib/user-interface), owns the SLeeLa DOM (SLGuiDom), the reconciler (SLGuiMount) that projects the DOM onto widgets, the host adapter (SLGuiHostAdapter) that raises widget activations back as events, and an optional script engine (SLGuiScript). SLGuiAudioCues #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiAudioCues.sleela)

SLGuiAudioCues class

Defines SLGuiAudioCues — the 3.0 activation-audio registry. UI components in the thual line may play a short audio CUE when activated (click/submit/toggle); this registry is the single place that names the available cues and the master audio settings, so an SLGuiEffects on a node references a cue by name and the host plays it through the audio stack. It holds a small bank of named cues (name -> host asset), a master enabled/mute flag, and a master gain. SLeeLa names and gates the cues; the host owns actual playback. Family: gui. Consulted by the host when a component with an activation cue fires; owned by SLGuiApp.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

cueAssetsString[] cueAssetshost-resolvable audio asset for the cue
cueCountint cueCountNo description in source.
enabledint enabled1 = activation audio is on globally
mutedint muted1 = temporarily silenced (enabled stays as-is)
masterGainPctint masterGainPct0..100 % master playback gain
playedint playedtotal cues dispatched to the host

SLGuiAudioCues #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-thual/SLGuiAudioCues.sleela)

SLGuiAudioCues class

Defines SLGuiAudioCues — the 3.0 activation-audio registry. UI components in the thual line may play a short audio CUE when activated (click/submit/toggle); this registry is the single place that names the available cues and the master audio settings, so an SLGuiEffects on a node references a cue by name and the host plays it through the audio stack. It holds a small bank of named cues (name -> host asset), a master enabled/mute flag, and a master gain. SLeeLa names and gates the cues; the host owns actual playback. Family: gui. Consulted by the host when a component with an activation cue fires; owned by SLGuiApp.

SLGuiAudioRecorder #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiAudioRecorder.sleela)

SLGuiAudioRecorder class

Defines SLGuiAudioRecorder — the 4.0 standard audio-input record control: a record button with the transport states a professional recorder needs (idle -> recording <-> paused -> stopped), an input device + format (sample rate, channels), a live input level, an elapsed duration, and an armed/monitoring flag. SLeeLa owns the recorder's STATE and the meaning of each transition; the host owns the actual capture device and writes the output asset. Every setting is validated/clamped. Family: gui. A control node's backing model; the host captures audio and reports level/duration back through this object.

SLGuiBranding class

Defines SLGuiBranding — the 3.0 logo + brand-identity surface for a SLeeLa GUI app: a logo asset (by host-resolvable name/path), a placement, a scale, an optional wordmark, brand accent/secondary colors, and a tagline. The host paints the logo into the chrome (title bar / splash / about / app header) at the requested placement and scale; SLeeLa names the brand, the host renders it. Every knob is validated/clamped. Family: gui. Owned by SLGuiApp; read by the host when it dresses the window.

SLGuiBridge #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiBridge.sleela)

SLGuiBridge class

SLGuiCertificateStore #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-military/SLGuiCertificateStore.sleela)

SLGuiCertificateStore class

Defines SLGuiCertificateStore — a military-line COMPONENT that holds and presents public-key certificates (an X.509-style store). Each entry carries a subject, an issuer, a key algorithm, a fingerprint, a trust state (trusted / untrusted / revoked / expired), and whether it is a CA. The store lets the program import a certificate, mark trust, select one for use, and query validity. SLeeLa owns the store CONTENTS and trust STATE; the host/crypto layer performs chain building and signature verification and reports the result back as a trust state. It is fail-closed: a certificate is untrusted until explicitly trusted, and a revoked/expired certificate is never reported valid. Family: gui. A "certstore" node's backing model; partners SLGuiCryptoSelector and SLGuiAdminAuthority (an admin signature for Law may reference a cert).

SLGuiClickObject #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiClickObject.sleela)

SLGuiClickObject class

Defines SLGuiClickObject — a 4.0 custom click object: a small circle with its own position, radius, architecturally-driven MOTION, and a staged TIMER. The timer runs through a sequence of "System Apprentice" stages — subtle, escalating activations — and when the final stage elapses it fires the FINAL CALL (a named SLeeLa operation). The motion is a declared architecture (static / drift / orbit / pulse) advanced by the app tick, so the circle moves predictably rather than by ad-hoc animation. SLeeLa owns position, motion, the apprentice ladder, and the final-call binding; the host paints the circle and plays any cue. The apprentice model: stage 0 is dormant; each interval advances one apprentice stage (subtle visual/behaviour change); reaching apprenticeMax triggers the final call exactly once. This gives a click object a careful, architecturally-driven build-up to its culminating action. Family: gui. A circle node's backing model; advanced by SLGuiApp's tick.

SLGuiCodecs #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiCodecs.sleela)

SLGuiCodecs class

Defines SLGuiCodecs — the GUI-facing view of the SLeeLa codec registry in /codecs. It mirrors codecs/include/sleela_codecs.h exactly (the 20 audio-codec ids, their capability STATE — native/backend/recognized/ container/event — MIME type, and file extensions) so GUI components can SEE what the system supports before offering media: a video canvas or audio recorder asks "can we play/record this?" and the URL bar / HTML renderer asks "is this <audio>/<source> type supported?". SLeeLa names the codecs here; the native /codecs backend (sleela_codec_* C ABI) does the actual encode/decode. Capability semantics (from codecs/CODECS.md): native = in-tree encode/ decode; backend = handler contract needs an approved library; recognized = identified only; container = carries audio but is not a codec; event = musical events, not PCM. "supported for playback" means native or backend. Family: gui. The SLeeLa-source mirror of /codecs; consulted by SLGuiVideoCanvas, SLGuiAudioRecorder, and SLGuiHtmlRenderer media elements.

SLGuiCryptoSelector #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-military/SLGuiCryptoSelector.sleela)

SLGuiCryptoSelector class

Defines SLGuiCryptoSelector — a military-line COMPONENT that lets a program choose its cryptography: a careful catalog of named suites (key-exchange + signature + cipher + hash), each with a security STRENGTH class (legacy / standard / strong / top-secret) so the UI can present and gate them. SLeeLa owns the catalog and the SELECTION; the host/crypto layer performs the actual cryptography. The selector is fail-closed: nothing is selected until an available suite is chosen, and a suite below a required minimum strength cannot be selected. The catalog names standards (not implementations) — e.g. AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, X25519, Ed25519, ML-KEM/ML-DSA (post-quantum). Listing a suite does not imply a bundled implementation; availability is reported separately so the component only offers what the platform can actually run. Family: gui. A "cryptoselector" node's backing model; the host supplies which suites are actually available and performs the selected cryptography.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

SLGuiDocument #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiDocument.sleela)

SLGuiDocument class

SLGuiDocumentListener #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiDocumentListener.sleela)

SLGuiDocumentListener class

Defines SLGuiDocumentListener — the SLeeLa GUI document-change listener option. Mirrors DocumentListener in gui/: watch 1..14 documents and refresh the running GUI whenever any changes on an OS call. Detection is OS-driven (WatchService over inotify / ReadDirectoryChangesW / kqueue/FSEvents), not polling; an OS event that does not move a document's revision is coalesced away. The 1..14 bound is a hard contract.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

SLGuiDom #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiDom.sleela)

SLGuiDom class

Defines SLGuiDom — the DHTML-style document model for /lib/gui: a flat registry of SLGuiNode elements forming a tree, plus the manipulation API a browser DOM exposes — createElement, getElementById, appendChild, removeChild, setText/setAttribute/setStyle on an id, show/hide, and a simple getElementsByTag / querySelector-by-attribute lookup. It owns an SLGuiEventBus so handlers bind to node ids (onClick, onInput, on(type,...), addEventListener) and raised events route to SLeeLa operations. The DOM is the single SLeeLa-owned source of truth; a host walks the dirty nodes and mirrors them onto real SleelaUI widgets. Family: gui. SLeeLa owns the document and dispatch; the host mounts and paints it.

SLGuiEffects #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiEffects.sleela)

SLGuiEffects class

Defines SLGuiEffects — the 3.0 (thual) per-component visual-effect bundle. A node may carry one of these to request clean, professional presentation the host renders onto the live widget: lighting + glow, a 3D shine highlight, a drop shadow, a metal look-and-feel, a rotation (fixed or on a schedule), and a fade in/out. Every knob is CLAMPED to a safe window, so a dialed value is never out of range, and toStyle() flattens the bundle into the node's inline-style map (effect-* properties) the SLGuiMount reconciler pushes to the toolkit. SLeeLa owns the intent; the host owns the pixels. The audio-on-activation hook is intentionally a NAME here (a cue the host plays through the audio stack); SLGuiEffects carries the cue + gain, not the sample. Rotation scheduling ("schene") is carried as an SLGuiRotationSchedule so a component can rotate on a cadence; see that class for the crypto-framed internal-memorandum rationale. Family: gui. Attached to SLGuiNode; flattened to style; realized by the host.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

Fields — the named values this unit stores.

FieldDeclarationWhat it holds
glowint glow--- lighting / glow --- 1 = glow enabled
glowRadiusPxint glowRadiusPxglow spread, 0..64 px
glowIntensityPctint glowIntensityPctglow strength, 0..100 %
glowColorString glowColor"#rrggbb" or a named accent ("accent"/"warning"/...)
shineint shine--- 3D shine highlight --- 1 = 3D specular shine enabled
shineAngleDegint shineAngleDeghighlight light angle, 0..359 deg
shineIntensityPctint shineIntensityPct0..100 %
shadowint shadow--- drop shadow --- 1 = shadow enabled
shadowOffsetXint shadowOffsetX-32..32 px
shadowOffsetYint shadowOffsetY-32..32 px
shadowBlurPxint shadowBlurPx0..64 px
shadowOpacityPctint shadowOpacityPct0..100 %
metalint metal--- metal look-and-feel --- 1 = brushed/metal surface enabled
metalSheenPctint metalSheenPct0..100 % (how reflective the surface reads)
rotationDegint rotationDeg--- rotation --- current fixed rotation, 0..359 deg
scheduleSLGuiRotationSchedule scheduleoptional scheduled "schene" rotation (null = static)
opacityPctint opacityPct--- fade --- 0..100 % current opacity
fadeMillisint fadeMillistransition duration for fade in/out, 0..10000 ms
activationCueString activationCue--- activation audio --- host audio cue name played on activation ("" = silent)
activationGainPctint activationGainPct0..100 % playback gain

Defines SLGuiEffects — the 3.0 (thual) per-component visual-effect bundle. A node may carry one of these to request clean, professional presentation the host renders onto the live widget: lighting + glow, a 3D shine highlight, a drop shadow, a metal look-and-feel, a rotation (fixed or on a schedule), and a fade in/out. Every knob is CLAMPED to a safe window, so a dialed value is never out of range, and toStyle() flattens the bundle into the node's inline-style map (effect-* properties) the SLGuiMount reconciler pushes to the toolkit. SLeeLa owns the intent; the host owns the pixels. The audio-on-activation hook is intentionally a NAME here (a cue the host plays through the audio stack); SLGuiEffects carries the cue + gain, not the sample. Rotation scheduling ("schene") is carried as an SLGuiRotationSchedule so a component can rotate on a cadence; see that class for the crypto-framed internal-memorandum rationale. Family: gui. Attached to SLGuiNode; flattened to style; realized by the host.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

SLGuiEvent #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiEvent.sleela)

SLGuiEvent class

Defines SLGuiEvent — one dispatched GUI event, the DHTML-style event object a handler receives. It names the event type (an SLGuiEventType ordinal), the target node id it was raised on, and the payload the kind carries: a string value (entry text / changed value), a key name (for key events), pointer coordinates (for pointer events), and a toggle state. It also carries the two propagation controls a handler can set — preventDefault() and stopPropagation() — exactly like a browser event, so SLeeLa handlers can cancel the host's default action or halt bubbling. Family: gui. The host raises the activation; SLeeLa reads this event and decides what it means.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

xint xpointer x within the target (pointer events)
yint ypointer y within the target (pointer events)

SLGuiEventBus #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiEventBus.sleela)

SLGuiEventBus class

Defines SLGuiEventBus — the event dispatcher and listener table for the /lib/gui event layer. It is the engine behind addEventListener / removeEventListener and the onClick/onInput shorthands: handlers register against a (type, target) pair, and dispatch(event) delivers a raised SLGuiEvent to every matching SLGuiHandler, honouring the DHTML-style phase order (capture handlers first, then target/bubble), stopPropagation() to halt delivery, and once handlers that auto-remove after firing. The bus is the SLeeLa-owned meaning layer: the host raises typed activations, the bus routes them to the bound operations. Family: gui. SLeeLa owns dispatch and the meaning of events; the host only raises them.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

The bus is the SLeeLa-owned meaning layer: the host raises typed activations, the bus routes them to the bound operations. Family: gui. SLeeLa owns dispatch and the meaning of events; the host only raises them.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

SLGuiEventType #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiEventType.sleela)

SLGuiEventType class

Defines SLGuiEventType — the catalogue of GUI event kinds the /lib/gui event layer understands. These are the SLeeLa-facing names a handler binds to (the DHTML-style "click", "input", "change", "keydown", ...). The host raises one of these on a target; SLeeLa decides what it means. Each kind has a stable ordinal (used by the dispatch tables) and a canonical lowercase name (the string an onX binding or addEventListener uses), mirroring the activation model already in SLGuiAction. Family: gui. Java/native raise typed activations; SLeeLa owns their meaning.

SLGuiGraphics #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiGraphics.sleela)

SLGuiGraphics class

Defines SLGuiGraphics — the 4.0 graphics facility AND its control layer for a canvas node. The facility is a bounded, auditable DRAW-COMMAND list (clear / line / rect / circle / arc / text / image) with stroke-width, fill/stroke colors, and opacity state; a command records the current state so the host replays the list deterministically. The control layer carries render quality, antialiasing, a layer index, and a dirty redraw region, so a program can tune how the facility is realised. SLeeLa owns the command list + control state; the host rasterises onto the real surface. This is a graphics *description*, not a general interpreter — a fixed verb set that can do no more than the canvas API allows. Family: gui. Backs a "canvas"/"graphics" node; replayed by the host renderer.

SLGuiHandler #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiHandler.sleela)

SLGuiHandler class

Defines SLGuiHandler — one registered event callback: the triple (event type, target node id, SLeeLa operation). It is the /lib/gui generalisation of SLGuiAction from a single click to any SLGuiEventType, and it is what addEventListener(target, type, operation) and the onClick/onInput shorthands create. When the dispatcher matches a raised SLGuiEvent to this handler it invokes the bound operation; the handler latches each fire so a host that polls (rather than calls back) still observes each activation exactly once, the same take-the-latch discipline as SLGuiAction. Family: gui. The host raises activations; this binding maps them to a SLeeLa operation whose meaning SLeeLa owns.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

FieldDeclarationWhat it holds
typeint typeSLGuiEventType ordinal this handler listens for
targetIdString targetIdnode id it is bound to ("*" matches any target)
operationString operationthe SLeeLa operation invoked when it fires
onceint once1 = auto-remove after the first fire
captureint capture1 = fire during capture phase, 0 = bubble phase
enabledint enabled1 while active
pendingint pendingactivation latch (set on fire, cleared on take)
firedint firedtotal times fired
lastValueString lastValuethe value carried by the most recent matching event

When the dispatcher matches a raised SLGuiEvent to this handler it invokes the bound operation; the handler latches each fire so a host that polls (rather than calls back) still observes each activation exactly once, the same take-the-latch discipline as SLGuiAction. Family: gui. The host raises activations; this binding maps them to a SLeeLa operation whose meaning SLeeLa owns.

SLGuiHostAdapter #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiHostAdapter.sleela)

SLGuiHostAdapter class

Defines SLGuiHostAdapter — the toolkit->SLeeLa half of the loop. Where SLGuiMount pushes DOM state onto widgets, the host adapter reads the widgets back: once per frame it polls each mounted interactive node's widget activation latch (uiWidgetTakeActivated, the same latch SLButton and SLEntry expose) and, when a widget fired, builds the matching SLGuiEvent (CLICK for a button, SUBMIT for an entry, TOGGLE for a toggle — carrying the widget's current text/toggle state as the event value) and dispatches it through the DOM's SLGuiEventBus so the bound onClick/onSubmit/onToggle handlers fire. This is what turns a real user interaction into a SLeeLa event; the DOM stays authoritative for what the event means. Family: gui. The adapter crosses the `ui*` SLVM bridge inbound; dispatch and meaning stay SLeeLa-owned.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

Fields — the named values this unit stores.

FieldDeclarationWhat it holds
domSLGuiDom domNo description in source.
mountSLGuiMount mountNo description in source.
factorySLGuiWidgetFactory factoryNo description in source.
tickint tickmonotonic frame counter stamped onto events
raisedLastint raisedLastevents raised on the last poll pass

Methods — the actions this unit can perform.

MethodSignatureWhat it does
initvoid init(SLGuiDom document, SLGuiMount mountEngine)No description in source.
pollint poll()Poll every mounted interactive node once; raise an SLGuiEvent for each that fired since the last poll. Returns the number of events dispatched.
raiseForvoid raiseFor(SLGuiNode node, int widgetHandle)Build and dispatch the event a fired widget implies.
raiseInputint raiseInput(String nodeId, String text)Also feed a synthetic input event (per-keystroke) for an entry, used by a host that wants live INPUT handlers in addition to the committed SUBMIT.
raisedCountint raisedCount()No description in source.
frameint frame()No description in source.

SLGuiIcon #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-military/SLGuiIcon.sleela)

SLGuiIcon class

Defines SLGuiIcon — a carefully sized, precisely placed icon that can be attached to a button, a menu item, or any clickable component. It carries an asset name, a size TIER (a small set of calm, matched sizes so icons read consistently across the UI rather than at arbitrary pixel sizes), a POSITION relative to the label (leading / trailing / top / icon- only), a gap between icon and label, a tint, and an optical-alignment nudge so an icon sits visually centred (not just geometrically). The point is aesthetic calm: every icon is one of a few matched sizes, placed perfectly for the component it rides on. Family: gui. Attached to a node (via SLGuiIconHost / effects) on buttons, menu items, and clickables; the host paints the asset at the computed rect.

SLGuiKind #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-military/SLGuiKind.sleela)

SLGuiKind class

Defines SLGuiKind — the explicit CONTAINER vs COMPONENT taxonomy for the military GUI line. Every node tag is classified as either a CONTAINER (it holds and lays out children — window, box, frame, header, status, grid) or a COMPONENT (a leaf control the user interacts with or reads — button, label, entry, toggle, recorder, video, urlbar, circle, canvas, html, crypto selector, certificate store, menu item). It also states which kinds may carry an ICON (buttons, menu items, and clickable components), so icons are only offered where they belong. This makes the distinction a first-class, queryable fact rather than something implied by the widget factory's construction branch. Family: gui. Pure classification; consulted by the factory, mount, and the icon system to decide layout role and icon eligibility.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

SLGuiLayout #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiLayout.sleela)

SLGuiLayout class

Defines SLGuiLayout — the 4.0 layout + exact-positioning surface. It lets a component be placed EXACTLY (absolute x/y/width/height in px) or be governed by a layout MODE (flow / grid / anchor / dock) with alignment, padding, and inter-child gap. It also carries anchor edges (left/top/right/ bottom) and a dock side so a child tracks its parent's resize predictably. SLeeLa declares the geometry intent precisely; the host realises it on the toolkit. Every value is validated/clamped; honored() checks consistency. Family: gui. Attached to a node (or a container) to drive placement; read by SLGuiMount when it positions the widget.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

SLGuiModal #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiModal.sleela)

SLGuiModal class

Defines SLGuiModal — the MODAL / OVERLAY component: a dialog that sits on top of the main application view and fades IN alongside a DARKENED backdrop (the scrim), then fades OUT on close. It is a pure model + lifecycle state machine: closed -> opening -> open -> closing -> closed, driven by tick(elapsed). The dialog and the scrim each fade through an SLGuiTransition (the scrim only to its target dim level, never fully opaque). SLeeLa owns the title, the dismiss policy, and the timing; the host paints the scrim over the view and the dialog over the scrim. Family: gui. A view-blocking overlay; this model decides when the dialog and its backdrop are visible and how opaque each is.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

Fields — the named values this unit stores.

FieldDeclarationWhat it holds
STATE_CLOSEDstatic final int STATE_CLOSED = 0Lifecycle states.
STATE_OPENINGstatic final int STATE_OPENING = 1enter transition running
STATE_OPENstatic final int STATE_OPEN = 2fully shown, awaiting dismissal
STATE_CLOSINGstatic final int STATE_CLOSING = 3exit transition running
titleString titleNo description in source.
stateint stateSTATE_*
scrimDimPctint scrimDimPctbackdrop darkness target, 0..100 % (how dark it gets)
dismissOnBackdropint dismissOnBackdrop1 = clicking the darkened backdrop closes it
dismissOnEscapeint dismissOnEscape1 = pressing Escape closes it
dialogFxSLGuiTransition dialogFxthe dialog's enter/exit fade (and scale feel)

SLGuiModal #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-gual/SLGuiModal.sleela)

SLGuiModal class

Defines SLGuiModal — the MODAL / OVERLAY component: a dialog that sits on top of the main application view and fades IN alongside a DARKENED backdrop (the scrim), then fades OUT on close. It is a pure model + lifecycle state machine: closed -> opening -> open -> closing -> closed, driven by tick(elapsed). The dialog and the scrim each fade through an SLGuiTransition (the scrim only to its target dim level, never fully opaque). SLeeLa owns the title, the dismiss policy, and the timing; the host paints the scrim over the view and the dialog over the scrim. Family: gui. A view-blocking overlay; this model decides when the dialog and its backdrop are visible and how opaque each is.

SLGuiMount #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiMount.sleela)

SLGuiMount class

Defines SLGuiMount — the reconciler that reflects the SLeeLa-owned DOM (SLGuiDom / SLGuiNode) onto real SleelaUI widgets. It mounts the tree depth-first (a parent is constructed before its children so each child has a real parent handle), records an id->widget-handle map, and on each pass applies every dirty node's state to its widget through the `ui*` built-ins: text (uiWidgetSetText), visibility (uiWidgetVisible), sensitivity (uiWidgetSensitive), and the style-derived accents (suggested/destructive) and minimum size. This is the one-way SLeeLa->toolkit half of the loop (SLGuiHostAdapter is the toolkit->SLeeLa half). The DOM stays the single source of truth; the widgets are its projection. Family: gui. The reconciler crosses the `ui*` SLVM bridge; SLeeLa owns the document it mirrors.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

MAX_NODESstatic final int MAX_NODES = 65536No description in source.
domSLGuiDom domNo description in source.
factorySLGuiWidgetFactory factoryNo description in source.
idsString[] idsid -> widget handle map (parallel arrays).
handlesint[] handlesNo description in source.
mapCountint mapCountNo description in source.

Methods — the actions this unit can perform.

MethodSignatureWhat it does
initvoid init(SLGuiDom document, int windowRootHandle)No description in source.
handleOfint handleOf(String id)No description in source.
mapIdvoid mapId(String id, int handle)No description in source.
indexOfint indexOf(String id)No description in source.
isMountedboolean isMounted(String id)No description in source.
mountAllvoid mountAll()Mount the whole document under the window root, depth-first.
mountChildrenvoid mountChildren(SLGuiNode parent)Recursively construct and mount every child of `parent`.
mountNewvoid mountNew()Mount any nodes added since the last pass (nodes the DOM grew via script or SLeeLa after the initial mountAll).
reconcileint reconcile()Push every dirty node's state onto its widget, then clear the dirty flag. Returns how many nodes were applied this pass.
applyvoid apply(SLGuiNode node)Apply one node's state to its live widget via the `ui*` built-ins.
mountedCountint mountedCount()No description in source.
appliedLastint appliedLast()No description in source.
constructWithOverflowint constructWithOverflow(int parentHandle, SLGuiNode child, String label)Construct a child's widget, honouring an `overflow` intent. A container whose tag is already a scrolled view (scrolled/scrollview/scrollarea) is built by the factory as usual. Otherwise, if the node carries an `overflow` attribute (or per-axis `overflow-x` / `overflow-y`), build a native scrolled viewport with the mapped policy instead of a plain container, so the content scrolls and scrollbars appear automatically on overflow. The node's children then mount inside the viewport as its scroll content. overflow / overflow-x / overflow-y : auto | scroll | always | hidden | visible | clip | none (auto is the default when the attr is present without a value). A per-axis attr overrides the shorthand for that axis.
labelForString labelFor(SLGuiNode node)The construction label for a node: its text, or its "placeholder" attr for entries, or empty.
intAttrint intAttr(String s)Parse a non-negative integer from a decimal string ("" / null -> 0).
digitint digit(String ch)No description in source.

A container whose tag is already a scrolled view (scrolled/scrollview/scrollarea) is built by the factory as usual. Otherwise, if the node carries an `overflow` attribute (or per-axis `overflow-x` / `overflow-y`), build a native scrolled viewport with the mapped policy instead of a plain container, so the content scrolls and scrollbars appear automatically on overflow. The node's children then mount inside the viewport as its scroll content. overflow / overflow-x / overflow-y : auto | scroll | always | hidden | visible | clip | none (auto is the default when the attr is present without a value). A per-axis attr overrides the shorthand for that axis.

SLGuiMount #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-mual/SLGuiMount.sleela)

SLGuiMount class

Defines SLGuiMount — the reconciler that reflects the SLeeLa-owned DOM (SLGuiDom / SLGuiNode) onto real SleelaUI widgets. It mounts the tree depth-first (a parent is constructed before its children so each child has a real parent handle), records an id->widget-handle map, and on each pass applies every dirty node's state to its widget through the `ui*` built-ins: text (uiWidgetSetText), visibility (uiWidgetVisible), sensitivity (uiWidgetSensitive), and the style-derived accents (suggested/destructive) and minimum size. This is the one-way SLeeLa->toolkit half of the loop (SLGuiHostAdapter is the toolkit->SLeeLa half). The DOM stays the single source of truth; the widgets are its projection. Family: gui. The reconciler crosses the `ui*` SLVM bridge; SLeeLa owns the document it mirrors.

SLGuiNode #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiNode.sleela)

SLGuiNode class

Defines SLGuiNode — a DHTML-style element node in the /lib/gui document model. Like a DOM element it has a tag (e.g. "window", "box", "button", "label", "entry"), a unique id, text content, a parent id, an ordered list of child ids, a flat attribute map, a flat style map, and a visibility/enabled state. SLeeLa code (or a script) manipulates the tree through these — setAttribute, setStyle, show/hide, enable/disable, setText — and the host reflects the node onto a real SleelaUI widget. A node carries an optional widget handle so a change can be pushed to the live control, but the node itself is the SLeeLa-owned source of truth. In the 3.0 (thual) line a node may also carry an SLGuiEffects bundle (lighting/glow, 3D shine, shadow, metal, rotation incl. scheduled "schene" rotation, fade in/out, activation audio); effects() lazily creates it and applyEffects() flattens it into the node's style for the reconciler. Family: gui. The DOM is SLeeLa-owned; the host mirrors it onto widgets.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

SLGuiRotationSchedule #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiRotationSchedule.sleela)

SLGuiRotationSchedule class

Defines SLGuiRotationSchedule — a "schene": a scheduled rotation cadence for a UI component. On its face it rotates a component by a fixed step every interval (a clean, professional motion accent). Its second, deliberate role is a CRYPTOGRAPHIC ROTATION CADENCE for an internal memorandum: the same tick that advances the visible angle also advances a key epoch, so "the component is rotating" and "the memo's internal key has rotated to a new epoch" are one observable event. The visible rotation is the honest, external signal of an internal key rotation — rotation you can see maps to rotation you can trust. This class carries ONLY the cadence/accounting (interval, step, epoch, bounded total turns); it does not implement a cipher. It states how often the memorandum's key epoch turns and lets a consumer read epoch()/turns() to drive the actual key schedule elsewhere. Every value is clamped. Family: gui. Carried by SLGuiEffects; advanced by the app/mount loop tick.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

Fields — the named values this unit stores.

FieldDeclarationWhat it holds
intervalMillisint intervalMillistime between rotation steps, 50..3600000 ms
stepDegint stepDegdegrees added each interval, -359..359
runningint running1 while the cadence advances
accumMillisint accumMilliselapsed time banked toward the next step
epochint epochkey epoch: increments once per completed step
turnsint turnstotal steps applied
maxTurnsint maxTurns0 = unbounded; else stop after maxTurns steps
memoLabelString memoLabelthe internal memorandum this cadence rotates the key for

SLGuiScript #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiScript.sleela)

SLGuiScript class

Defines SLGuiScript — the scripting engine for /lib/gui. It holds an ordered list of SLGuiScriptCommands and runs them against an SLGuiDom (and, for the `call` verb, across the native boundary via SLGuiBridge). This is the "support for scripting" layer: a UI can be described and driven by a command list rather than hand-written SLeeLa, which is what makes DHTML-style authoring and tooling (serialising a UI, replaying interactions, data-driven screens) possible. The engine is deliberately NOT a general interpreter — it is a bounded, auditable verb list that only touches the SLeeLa-owned DOM/event bus and the documented operation bridge, so a script can never do more than the DOM API already allows. Family: gui. SLeeLa owns execution; scripts express UI intent declaratively.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

SLGuiScriptCommand #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiScriptCommand.sleela)

SLGuiScriptCommand class

Defines SLGuiScriptCommand — one instruction of a /lib/gui UI script. The scripting support is a small, safe, declarative command list (not an arbitrary interpreter): each command is a verb plus up to four string operands. The verbs mirror the DOM/event API so a script can build and drive an interface without native code — create, append, text, attr, style, show, hide, enable, on (bind a handler), fire (raise an event), and call (cross the native bridge to a SLeeLa operation). An ordinal verb keeps dispatch cheap; the operands are interpreted per verb by SLGuiScript. Family: gui. Scripts describe UI intent; SLeeLa (via SLGuiScript) executes it against the SLeeLa-owned DOM and event bus.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

SLGuiScriptCommand #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-mual/SLGuiScriptCommand.sleela)

SLGuiScriptCommand class

Defines SLGuiScriptCommand — one instruction of a /lib/gui UI script. The scripting support is a small, safe, declarative command list (not an arbitrary interpreter): each command is a verb plus up to four string operands. The verbs mirror the DOM/event API so a script can build and drive an interface without native code — create, append, text, attr, style, show, hide, enable, on (bind a handler), fire (raise an event), and call (cross the native bridge to a SLeeLa operation). An ordinal verb keeps dispatch cheap; the operands are interpreted per verb by SLGuiScript. Family: gui. Scripts describe UI intent; SLeeLa (via SLGuiScript) executes it against the SLeeLa-owned DOM and event bus.

SLGuiScrollbar #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiScrollbar.sleela)

SLGuiScrollbar class

Defines SLGuiScrollbar — the IMPLIED scrollbar model for a scrolled surface, in BOTH axes (vertical and horizontal). It is a pure model: given a viewport extent and the content extent on an axis, it decides whether a scrollbar is IMPLIED (content overflows the viewport), and computes the two normalized [0,1] values the toolkit's drawn scroll bar needs — `page` (the fraction of content the viewport shows, i.e. the thumb size) and `value` (the thumb position from the current scroll offset). It also resolves a visibility policy (auto / always / never) so a host can show the bar only when scrolling is actually implied. SLeeLa owns the geometry + policy; the host paints it with `uiScrollBar(parent, orient, value, page)` and feeds scroll gestures back through `scrollBy` / `scrollTo`. Family: gui. The companion of SLGuiLayout for overflow; the drawn bar is the existing SleelaUI scroll-bar control — this class is the implied geometry.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

SHOW_AUTOstatic final int SHOW_AUTO = 0Visibility policy for an implied scrollbar. shown only while content overflows
SHOW_ALWAYSstatic final int SHOW_ALWAYS = 1always shown (reserves the gutter)
SHOW_NEVERstatic final int SHOW_NEVER = 2never shown (overflow still scrolls)

SLGuiSettings class

Defines SLGuiSettings — the 2.0 (gual) settings surface for the SLeeLa GUI package. Where the 1.0 (mual) line scattered a few tunables across classes, 2.0 gathers the operating knobs into one validated, nameful object: presentation (theme, DPI scale, reduced-motion / accessibility, vsync), window defaults (min/max size, resizable, decorations), and the document-listener timing (poll cadence, debounce window, coalesce-queue cap, backpressure policy). Every setting is CLAMPED to a safe window when applied — a dialed value is never accepted outside its stated range, and honored()/report() say whether the configuration is internally consistent. This mirrors the quality-first, clamp-to-window discipline used by the lib/cpu timing/voltage layer. Family: gui. A plain settings object; read by SLGuiBackend / SLGuiWindow / SLGuiDocumentListener and by SLGuiApp at boot.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

BACKPRESSURE_COALESCEstatic final int BACKPRESSURE_COALESCE = 0--- document-listener backpressure policy --- merge overflow into the latest (default)

SLGuiSkeleton #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiSkeleton.sleela)

SLGuiSkeleton class

Defines SLGuiSkeleton — the SKELETON SCREEN / PLACEHOLDER component: a subtle panel that fades IN to stand in for content that is still loading, animates a gentle shimmer/pulse while it waits, and then DISSOLVES to reveal the real content once loading completes. It is a pure model + lifecycle state machine: idle -> loading(shimmer) -> revealing -> revealed, driven by tick(elapsed). The initial appearance and the reveal cross-fade are SLGuiTransitions; the shimmer is a looping 0..100..0 pulse. SLeeLa owns the shape (how many placeholder lines/blocks) and the timing; the host paints the grey blocks, the moving shimmer, and the reveal. Family: gui. A loading placeholder; this model decides shimmer phase, panel opacity, and when the real content is revealed.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

Fields — the named values this unit stores.

STATE_IDLEstatic final int STATE_IDLE = 0Lifecycle states. not shown
STATE_LOADINGstatic final int STATE_LOADING = 1placeholder visible, shimmering
STATE_REVEALINGstatic final int STATE_REVEALING = 2cross-fading placeholder -> content
STATE_REVEALEDstatic final int STATE_REVEALED = 3real content shown, placeholder gone
SHAPE_TEXTstatic final int SHAPE_TEXT = 0Placeholder shape presets (host maps to a block layout). stacked text lines
SHAPE_CARDstatic final int SHAPE_CARD = 1media block + text lines
SHAPE_AVATARstatic final int SHAPE_AVATAR = 2circle + two short lines
SHAPE_LISTstatic final int SHAPE_LIST = 3repeated rows

linesint linesnumber of placeholder blocks/rows, 1..32

shimmerPeriodMsint shimmerPeriodMsone full shimmer sweep, 200..10000 ms
shimmerElapsedint shimmerElapsedposition within the current sweep

revealFxSLGuiTransition revealFxthe placeholder -> content dissolve (cross-fade)

SLGuiToast #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiToast.sleela)

SLGuiToast class

Defines SLGuiToast — the TOAST / SNACKBAR component: a small notification panel that fades IN at a corner/edge of the screen, DWELLS for a few seconds, then fades OUT. It is a pure model + lifecycle state machine: hidden -> fadingIn -> shown -> fadingOut -> hidden, driven by tick(elapsed). The fade in and fade out are each an SLGuiTransition (the shared enter/exit tween); the dwell is a plain timer. SLeeLa owns the message, placement, severity, and timing; the host paints the panel at the resolved opacity and anchors it to the chosen corner. Family: gui. A self-dismissing notification; the host renders it, this model decides when it is visible and how opaque.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

Fields — the named values this unit stores.

FieldDeclarationWhat it holds
STATE_HIDDENstatic final int STATE_HIDDEN = 0Lifecycle states. not on screen
STATE_FADING_INstatic final int STATE_FADING_IN = 1enter transition running
STATE_SHOWNstatic final int STATE_SHOWN = 2fully visible, dwelling
STATE_FADING_OUTstatic final int STATE_FADING_OUT = 3exit transition running
SEV_INFOstatic final int SEV_INFO = 0Severity (tints the panel; the host maps to accent/warning/danger/success).
SEV_SUCCESSstatic final int SEV_SUCCESS = 1No description in source.
SEV_WARNINGstatic final int SEV_WARNING = 2No description in source.
SEV_DANGERstatic final int SEV_DANGER = 3No description in source.
POS_TOP_LEFTstatic final int POS_TOP_LEFT = 0Placement anchors (which screen corner/edge the toast docks to).
POS_TOP_RIGHTstatic final int POS_TOP_RIGHT = 1No description in source.
POS_TOP_CENTERstatic final int POS_TOP_CENTER = 2No description in source.
POS_BOTTOM_LEFTstatic final int POS_BOTTOM_LEFT = 3No description in source.
POS_BOTTOM_RIGHTstatic final int POS_BOTTOM_RIGHT = 4No description in source.
POS_BOTTOM_CENTERstatic final int POS_BOTTOM_CENTER = 5No description in source.

SLGuiToast #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-mual/SLGuiToast.sleela)

SLGuiToast class

Defines SLGuiToast — the TOAST / SNACKBAR component: a small notification panel that fades IN at a corner/edge of the screen, DWELLS for a few seconds, then fades OUT. It is a pure model + lifecycle state machine: hidden -> fadingIn -> shown -> fadingOut -> hidden, driven by tick(elapsed). The fade in and fade out are each an SLGuiTransition (the shared enter/exit tween); the dwell is a plain timer. SLeeLa owns the message, placement, severity, and timing; the host paints the panel at the resolved opacity and anchors it to the chosen corner. Family: gui. A self-dismissing notification; the host renders it, this model decides when it is visible and how opaque.

SLGuiTransition #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiTransition.sleela)

SLGuiTransition class

Defines SLGuiTransition — the FADING-ACTION model (an "enter" / "exit" transition, a.k.a. intro/outro animation). It is a pure model: given a start and end opacity (the CSS `opacity` property, 0..100 %), a duration (the tween window), an easing curve, and an optional start delay, it tweens ("in-betweens") the current opacity for a given elapsed time. SLeeLa owns the curve + timing; the host realizes it with a CSS `transition` / `@keyframes` (or a toolkit animator) using the descriptor from toStyle(). Terms (documentation labels): the component that fades is a Toast/Snackbar, Modal/Overlay, Transition-wrapper, or Skeleton; the ACTION here is the enter transition / tween / dissolve; the CSS surface is opacity + transition + @keyframes. This class is the reusable fade primitive the GUI components (SLGuiToast / SLGuiModal / SLGuiSkeleton) embed. Family: gui. A pure tween model (ints only); the host paints the pixels.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

Fields — the named values this unit stores.

FieldDeclarationWhat it holds
KIND_ENTERstatic final int KIND_ENTER = 0Direction of the transition. fade/scale IN (opacity rises to target)
KIND_EXITstatic final int KIND_EXIT = 1fade/scale OUT (opacity falls to target)
EASE_LINEARstatic final int EASE_LINEAR = 0Easing curves (how the tween accelerates). Mirrors the common CSS set plus a film/game "dissolve" (a smooth cross-fade feel == ease-in-out here). constant rate
EASE_INstatic final int EASE_IN = 1starts slow, speeds up
EASE_OUTstatic final int EASE_OUT = 2starts fast, slows down
EASE_IN_OUTstatic final int EASE_IN_OUT = 3slow, fast, slow
EASE_DISSOLVEstatic final int EASE_DISSOLVE = 4seamless cross-fade (== in-out feel)
PCTstatic final int PCT = 100Opacity is carried in PERCENT (0..100); progress in PERMILLE (0..1000) so the model stays integer-only (SLeeLa ints). Callers divide by 100.0 / 1000.0 when they need the [0,1] double a toolkit wants.
UNITstatic final int UNIT = 1000No description in source.
kindint kindKIND_ENTER / KIND_EXIT
easingint easingEASE_*
fromPctint fromPctstart opacity, 0..100
toPctint toPctend opacity, 0..100
durationMsint durationMstween duration, 0..60000 ms
delayMsint delayMsstart delay before the tween begins, 0..60000 ms
elapsedMsint elapsedMstime advanced so far (clamped to delay+duration)

Methods — the actions this unit can perform.

MethodSignatureWhat it does
clampint clamp(int v, int lo, int hi)No description in source.
configurevoid configure()Safe defaults: a 200 ms ease-out fade-in from fully transparent to opaque.
fadeInvoid fadeIn(int ms, int ease)Configure a fade-IN (enter): 0 -> 100 % over `ms` with `ease`.
fadeOutvoid fadeOut(int ms, int ease)Configure a fade-OUT (exit): 100 -> 0 % over `ms` with `ease`.
betweenvoid between(int kindVal, int fromOpacityPct, int toOpacityPct, int ms, int ease)A general enter/exit between arbitrary opacities.
setEasingvoid setEasing(int ease)No description in source.
setDelayvoid setDelay(int ms)No description in source.
setDurationvoid setDuration(int ms)No description in source.
resetvoid reset()---- playback -----------------------------------------------------------
advancevoid advance(int deltaMs)Advance the tween by `deltaMs`; clamps to the delay+duration window.
doneboolean done()The tween is finished once the whole delay+duration window has elapsed.
rawProgressPermilleint rawProgressPermille()Linear progress through the active (post-delay) window, in permille 0..1000.
easeProgressint easeProgress(int p)Apply the easing curve to a linear permille progress. Integer-only: ease-in : p^2 (slow start) ease-out : 1-(1-p)^2 (slow end) in-out : piecewise quadratic (slow start & end) dissolve : == in-out (seamless cross-fade feel)
progressPermilleint progressPermille()The eased progress (permille) at the current elapsed time.
opacityPctint opacityPct()The current tweened opacity in PERCENT (0..100), interpolating from->to by the eased progress. This is the value the host writes to CSS `opacity`.
opacityAtint opacityAt(int atElapsedMs)Convenience: the opacity at an explicit elapsed time (does not mutate state).

SLGuiTransition #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-thual/SLGuiTransition.sleela)

SLGuiTransition class

Defines SLGuiTransition — the FADING-ACTION model (an "enter" / "exit" transition, a.k.a. intro/outro animation). It is a pure model: given a start and end opacity (the CSS `opacity` property, 0..100 %), a duration (the tween window), an easing curve, and an optional start delay, it tweens ("in-betweens") the current opacity for a given elapsed time. SLeeLa owns the curve + timing; the host realizes it with a CSS `transition` / `@keyframes` (or a toolkit animator) using the descriptor from toStyle(). Terms (documentation labels): the component that fades is a Toast/Snackbar, Modal/Overlay, Transition-wrapper, or Skeleton; the ACTION here is the enter transition / tween / dissolve; the CSS surface is opacity + transition + @keyframes. This class is the reusable fade primitive the GUI components (SLGuiToast / SLGuiModal / SLGuiSkeleton) embed. Family: gui. A pure tween model (ints only); the host paints the pixels.

SLGuiUrlBar #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiUrlBar.sleela)

SLGuiUrlBar class

Defines SLGuiUrlBar — the 4.0 HTML-aware, HTTP-driven URL navigation bar: an address field with go / back / forward / reload / stop, a bounded navigation history, the current load state, and the HTTP facts of the last navigation (method, status, content-type, secure flag). It is "HTML-aware" in that it recognises an HTML response (so the host renders it into the DOM/canvas) vs. a non-HTML resource. SLeeLa owns the navigation STATE and history; the host performs the actual HTTP fetch and reports the result back. URLs are validated (scheme + non-empty host). Family: gui. Backs a URL-bar node; the host fetches and feeds back status.

SLGuiVideoCanvas #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiVideoCanvas.sleela)

SLGuiVideoCanvas class

Defines SLGuiVideoCanvas — the 4.0 video surface for playing movies with a full set of transport controls: a source asset, play / pause / stop / seek, a position and duration (ms), volume + mute, loop, playback rate, and a fullscreen flag. SLeeLa owns the player STATE and the meaning of each control; the host decodes and presents the frames onto the canvas widget and reports position back. Every setting is validated/clamped so a seek or volume is never out of range. Family: gui. A canvas node's backing model; the host renders video + audio and reports playback position/buffering to this object.

SLGuiVideoCanvas #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-military/SLGuiVideoCanvas.sleela)

SLGuiVideoCanvas class

Defines SLGuiVideoCanvas — the 4.0 video surface for playing movies with a full set of transport controls: a source asset, play / pause / stop / seek, a position and duration (ms), volume + mute, loop, playback rate, and a fullscreen flag. SLeeLa owns the player STATE and the meaning of each control; the host decodes and presents the frames onto the canvas widget and reports position back. Every setting is validated/clamped so a seek or volume is never out of range. Family: gui. A canvas node's backing model; the host renders video + audio and reports playback position/buffering to this object.

SLGuiWidgetFactory #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiWidgetFactory.sleela)

SLGuiWidgetFactory class

Defines SLGuiWidgetFactory — the single place that knows how a DOM tag maps to a real SleelaUI widget. Given a node's tag and a parent widget handle it calls the matching `ui*` built-in (uiBox / uiButton / uiLabel / uiEntry / uiToggle / uiHeaderBar / uiStatusBar / ...) and returns the new widget handle, so the reconciler (SLGuiMount) never hard-codes toolkit knowledge. Tags mirror the SleelaUI vocabulary; an unknown tag falls back to a vertical box so an unrecognised element still has a container to hold children. This is the DOM->toolkit construction seam. Family: gui. The factory crosses the `ui*` SLVM bridge to the real toolkit; SLeeLa still owns the node that the widget mirrors.

Carries the standard Metadata Class record — eleven catalogued provenance attributes (version, id, author, date, copyright, trademark, corporation, origin, birth date, science rating, national schedule) with matching get/set accessors. These are omitted from the tables below for brevity.

Fields — the named values this unit stores.

FieldDeclarationWhat it holds
ORIENT_VERTICALstatic final int ORIENT_VERTICAL = 0Orientation ordinals (mirror SLUIOrientation / SLWidget).
ORIENT_HORIZONTALstatic final int ORIENT_HORIZONTAL = 1No description in source.
SCROLL_AUTOstatic final int SCROLL_AUTO = 0Scroll-visibility policy ordinals (mirror native ScrolledView::Policy and SLGuiScrollbar.SHOW_*): a scrolled viewport shows each axis' bar AUTO (only on overflow), ALWAYS, or NEVER.
SCROLL_ALWAYSstatic final int SCROLL_ALWAYS = 1No description in source.
SCROLL_NEVERstatic final int SCROLL_NEVER = 2No description in source.

Methods — the actions this unit can perform.

MethodSignatureWhat it does
overflowPolicyint overflowPolicy(String kw)Map a CSS-style overflow keyword to a scroll policy. "auto"/"" -> AUTO, "scroll"/"always" -> ALWAYS, "hidden"/"visible"/"clip"/"none" -> NEVER.
constructScrolledint constructScrolled(int parentHandle, int policyH, int policyV)Construct a scrolled viewport directly with explicit per-axis policies. SLGuiMount calls this to promote a container carrying an `overflow` attr.
isScrolledboolean isScrolled(String tag)Does this tag build a native scrolled viewport (first child = content)?
constructint construct(int parentHandle, String tag, String label)Construct the widget for `node` inside `parentHandle`. Returns the new widget handle, or -1 when it could not be created. `label` is the node's initial text/placeholder (empty string when it has none).
interactiveboolean interactive(String tag)Is this tag an interactive control the host should poll for activations?
activationEventint activationEvent(String tag)Which SLGuiEventType an activation on this tag should raise. Buttons -> CLICK; entries -> SUBMIT (Enter); toggles -> TOGGLE; the 4.0 surfaces raise CLICK (recorder/video/circle) or SUBMIT (urlbar go).
isContainerboolean isContainer(String tag)No description in source.

SLGuiWindow #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLGuiWindow.sleela)

SLGuiWindow class

Defines SLGuiWindow — a toolkit-neutral window intent. Mirrors the SleelaGui contract in gui/: show(title, width, height), setText(text), and refresh(documentId, revision). SLeeLa describes the window; the backend (Swing/JavaFX/native) renders it and marshals updates onto the toolkit thread.

SLGuiWindowState #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-military/SLGuiWindowState.sleela)

SLGuiWindowState class

Defines SLGuiWindowState — the military-line window-state machine and key-listener surface. It tracks the window mode (normal / minimized / fullscreen / maximized / FOLDED-to-a-desktop-side) and handles the gestures a host raises: resize, minimize, fullscreen, and "minimize right" — a FOLD of the UI to the right side of the desktop windowing area (also left, top, bottom). It remembers the previous "norm" geometry so a DOUBLE-CLICK restores the window to exactly what it was before it folded/minimized/ maximized. SLeeLa owns the state transitions + remembered norm; the host raises the key/gesture events and applies the resulting geometry. Family: gui. Backs SLGuiWindow's lifecycle; the host feeds gestures in and reads the resolved mode + target geometry out.

SLPackage #sleela 2.5 (lib/gui/version-dual/SLPackage.sleela)

SLPackage class

Defines the SLeeLa standard-library package for gui — the dual line (version 4.0). It builds on thual (3.0) and adds a rich, professional component set: an audio-input recorder, a video canvas with transport controls, an HTML-aware HTTP-driven URL navigation bar, custom click objects (motion + timers that escalate to System Apprentices), exact component positioning + strong layout support, a graphics facility and control, and an admin authority surface (sign-off on operations, sign-in to start a process, legal signature), with a substantially upgraded aesthetic.
